# Munder Difflin

> Munder Difflin gives you clones for you and your team, working 24/7. It is a free,
> MIT-licensed, local-first multi-agent harness for CLI coding agents that turns Claude Code,
> OpenAI Codex, Antigravity (Gemini), GitHub Copilot CLI, xAI Grok, Kimi Code, Qwen, OpenCode,
> Crush, Gemini CLI, Cursor Agent, and pi.dev into a coordinated "office" of agents on
> your own computer — each agent a real CLI process in a real terminal, with shared
> long-term memory, inter-agent messaging, your clone ("Michael") orchestrating, scheduled missions, Slack
> and webhook triggers, realtime voice orchestration, a built-in Monaco IDE with git
> history and branch compare, markdown previews, and auto-update. The interface runs in
> English, Simplified Chinese and Arabic, with right to left layout when Arabic is chosen,
> and its fonts are bundled rather than fetched from a font host. Current version: 0.4.6
> (August 2026). Desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. No vendor cloud; code never
> leaves your machine. It covers the same jobs as YC's qm (security postures, background
> crons/watches, Slack, shared skills) as a simpler local-first desktop app, and adds what
> a headless harness doesn't have: watchable terminals, voice, an IDE, auto-update.

### internals

- [The Spend Counter That Went Back to Zero](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/the-spend-counter-that-went-back-to-zero/): Our own floor was under reporting what it cost by 59 percent. The counter was cumulative since process start, the app restarts, and the session id stayed the same. Here is how a monotonic invariant let us recover the real number from an append-only log.
- [The Newline That Silenced Every Windows Agent](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/the-newline-that-silenced-windows-agents/): A cmd.exe parsing rule from the 1980s meant Windows agents received exactly one line of their multi-line startup protocol — and nothing errored. The anatomy of our worst silent failure, and the fix.
- [Our Auto-Update Never Ran Once: A CommonJS Export That Vanished Into an ESM Namespace](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/why-our-auto-update-never-ran/): Munder Difflin shipped auto-update in v0.3.4 and it silently never worked in a single packaged build. The cause was one destructuring assignment across the CommonJS/ESM boundary — and a catch block that threw the evidence away. Here's how we found it, and what v0.3.7 changes.
- [Treating a Hire Manifest as Untrusted Input](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/hire-manifest-untrusted-input/): A shareable agent-config manifest is attacker input. How Munder Difflin's import pipeline stays inert: no auto-spawn, default-deny flags, and an SSRF-safe bounded fetch.
- [Compressing Agent Memory Without Losing the Original](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/compressing-agent-memory/): How and why to compress an agent's long-term memory: the toolbox, the lossy trap, and keeping a lossless original beside a compact copy.
- [Munder Difflin's Architecture: Two Data Planes, One Renderer](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/architecture-two-planes-one-renderer/): A walkthrough of the multi-agent harness architecture: a node-pty terminal plane and a hooks/hive event plane feeding one React + Pixi.js renderer.
- [File-Based Coordination vs Message Queues for AI Agents](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/file-based-coordination-vs-message-queues/): Why a local agent hive coordinates through plain files, not Redis or RabbitMQ: the zero-ops wins, the real tradeoffs, and where files hit a ceiling.
- [Observability for Agent Fleets: Seeing What Your Agents Do](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/observability-for-agent-fleets/): Agent fleet observability: the four questions your dashboard must answer about who's working, what they're doing, what it costs, and what they know.
- [Recovering From Agent Failures: Resilience Patterns for a Hive](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/recovering-from-agent-failures/): How multi-agent systems survive partial failure: retry with stale-lock recovery, poison-message quarantine, hop-cap circuit breaking, idempotent handling.
- [The Hook Shim Pattern: Wiring Agent Hooks to a Live Process](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/the-hook-shim-pattern/): How a tiny shim bridges Claude Code's lifecycle hooks to one live process over a Unix socket, turning per-event hooks into a telemetry and control channel.
- [Building a Terminal UI with xterm.js and node-pty](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/building-a-terminal-ui-xterm-node-pty/): Wire xterm.js to a node-pty backend: stream output, write keystrokes back, handle resize, and keep many live terminals fast with a terminal pool.
- [Building an AI "Office Floor": Avatars, Pathfinding, Envelopes](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/building-an-ai-office-floor/): The game-dev techniques behind a dev tool's office floor: Tiled maps, BFS pathfinding, sprite recoloring, and flying message envelopes in Pixi.js.
- [Claude Code Hooks Explained: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and Exit Codes](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/claude-code-hooks-explained/): How Claude Code hooks work in 2026: the 33 events, where settings go, matcher syntax, exit code 2, and tested PreToolUse and Stop hook examples.
- [Real Terminals in Electron with node-pty](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/node-pty-electron-real-terminals/): How to run byte-for-byte authentic shells inside Electron with node-pty: the native-rebuild gotcha, the macOS PATH trap, and streaming PTY output over IPC.
- [Rendering Many Live Terminals Without Melting the CPU](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/rendering-many-live-terminals-performance/): xterm.js performance for many live PTYs: a terminal pool, render-only-visible, smart scrollback, and accelerated rendering to stream dozens at once.
- [The Single-Committer Pattern: Multi-Agent Git Without Corruption](https://munderdiffl.in/blog/single-committer-git-pattern/): Parallel agents corrupt a repo with index.lock races. The single-committer pattern — agents write, one process commits — fixes concurrent git writes.
